Lower unit repair: seals, bearings, shifting, milky gear oil

Milky gear oil, a grinding shift, a whine at speed, or a prop shaft that wobbles means the gearcase needs attention before it needs replacement. Mobile mechanics can pull a lower unit at your dock and reseal or rebuild it.

When
Milky or metallic gear oil, water in the oil at service time, hard or grinding shifting, fishing line around the prop shaft.
Time on site
2 to 3 hours for seals; rebuilds go to a bench
What it usually costs here
$400 to $900 for a reseal with pressure test; $1,500 to $3,500 for a rebuild depending on engine; a replacement gearcase can exceed that.

What's included

  • Gear oil drain and inspection for water and metal
  • Pressure and vacuum test of the gearcase
  • Prop shaft and drive shaft seal replacement
  • Shift shaft seal, water pump housing seal
  • Bearing and gear inspection, rebuild quote if needed
  • Prop and hub inspection, spline grease

In Tampa Bay specifically

Shallow flats off Anclote, Hudson, and the Pasco coast eat skegs and props. Grounding damage often shows up later as a seal leak.

Engines

  • Yamaha
  • Mercury
  • Suzuki
  • Honda Marine
  • Tohatsu

Questions we get

Why does fishing line matter?

Line cuts the prop shaft seal. Water gets in, bearings rust, and a $50 seal becomes a $2,500 rebuild. Check behind the prop every few trips.

Can the gearcase be pulled while the boat is on the lift?

Usually yes, with the engine tilted and the boat raised enough to clear.
